name: Other apps' data
plain: Each app's files and memory are sealed from other apps on both platforms.
meaning: Sandboxing keeps one app from reading another's messages, tokens or files. Only user-picked files, shared groups or content providers cross the line.

android.api_surface: App-private storage; scoped storage since Android 10, enforced 11
android.note: Sharing needs content providers or the Storage Access Framework

ios.api_surface: App sandbox container; app groups only for the same team
ios.note: Sharing needs app groups or file pickers

limits.headline: Can't open another app's files, messages or saved logins
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is blocked by the phone itself
can: See a file you pick through the file picker and share to it
Share data through a group or shared area that the same company set up
Receive what another app sends on purpose
cannot: See another app's messages, tokens or files on its own
Break the barrier between apps without rooting or jailbreaking the phone
limits.differs: Android shares through content providers or the file picker. iPhone shares through app groups or file pickers.

story.what_it_is: Blocked: one app cannot read another app's files, messages or saved logins.

marketing.name: App Sandbox on iOS
marketing.pitch: Each app runs in its own protected space so it cannot access other apps' data.

story.for_you: You do not see anything. It is the reason a game cannot read your banking app or your messages. Only things you pick, like a photo, cross between apps.
story.for_makers: Makers want to read other apps' data for ads, fraud scoring and rich features, but the system blocks it. They use approved bridges instead: share sheets, file pickers, shared app groups and sign in tokens.

use_cases.example: A budgeting app asks you to log in through your bank's own sign in because it cannot reach the bank app's data.
A photo editor cannot read your WhatsApp chats. You must choose a picture to share.
A game cannot copy your save from a rival game. Players must use cloud saves or accounts.
An ad SDK wanted other apps' ad history, but sandboxing forces it to use only its own data.
Malware that infects one app cannot jump into a password manager's vault.
Two apps from the same maker share data through a special shared container, with the person's knowledge.

story.android_note: Android runs each app as its own user and added scoped storage in 10 and 11.
story.ios_note: iOS keeps each app in a sealed container and only allows shared groups from one developer.
